documents.title: Programming fundamentals
documents.text: Programming fundamentals. Also known as: intro to programming, learn to code, coding basics, programming basics, introduction to computer programming, beginner coding. Core ideas shared by all programming languages: variables, data types, conditionals, loops, functions, and basic debugging. Once learned, you can break a small problem into steps and write simple working programs.

documents.title: Python
documents.text: Python. Also known as: python3, python programming, py, python language, learn python. The Python programming language: its syntax, built-in data types, functions, modules, classes, and standard library. Once learned, you can write and run scripts and small programs to automate tasks and solve everyday problems.

documents.title: JavaScript
documents.text: JavaScript. Also known as: js, ecmascript, es6, vanilla js, javascript programming. The core JavaScript language: variables, functions, objects, arrays, scope, classes and modules. A learner can write programs that run in the browser or on a server and manipulate data and the page.

documents.title: TypeScript
documents.text: TypeScript. Also known as: ts, typed javascript, tsc, typescript types, static typing for javascript. TypeScript is JavaScript with a static type system. It covers type annotations, interfaces, generics, and compiler configuration, so you can write safer, more maintainable JavaScript and catch bugs before runtime.

documents.title: Asynchronous JavaScript
documents.text: Asynchronous JavaScript. Also known as: async await, promises, async js, callbacks, event loop, async/await. The part of JavaScript that deals with code that runs later: callbacks, promises, async/await and the event loop. Once learned, you can fetch data, handle errors and sequence or parallelise asynchronous tasks without blocking.

documents.title: Java
documents.text: Java. Also known as: java programming, java se, jdk, java language, core java, jvm. The Java programming language and its core platform: syntax, classes and interfaces, collections, exceptions, generics, and the JVM. Once learned, you can write, build and run structured Java programs and use the standard library.

documents.title: Go (Golang)
documents.text: Go (Golang). Also known as: golang, go language, go programming, go lang. The Go programming language: its syntax, types, structs and interfaces, error handling, goroutines and channels, and standard tooling. Once learned, you can build and test simple command-line tools and network services in idiomatic Go.

documents.title: Rust
documents.text: Rust. Also known as: rust lang, rustlang, cargo, borrow checker, rustc. A systems programming language focused on memory safety without garbage collection. Covers ownership, borrowing, lifetimes, traits, error handling and Cargo, so you can build fast, reliable command-line tools and services.

documents.title: SQL
documents.text: SQL. Also known as: structured query language, sql queries, database queries, select statements, t-sql. Writing queries to retrieve, filter, join, aggregate and modify data in relational databases. Once learned, you can answer questions from tables using SELECT, JOINs, GROUP BY and subqueries, and insert, update and delete records.

documents.title: PostgreSQL
documents.text: PostgreSQL. Also known as: postgres, psql, pg, postgres database, pgsql. PostgreSQL is a specific open-source relational database system built on SQL. Covers installing and administering it, its data types (JSONB, arrays), indexes, query planning, transactions, and extensions, so you can run and tune a Postgres database.

documents.title: Relational database design
documents.text: Relational database design. Also known as: database design, schema design, database normalization, data modeling, er diagrams, entity relationship modeling, normal forms. Covers designing relational schemas: modeling entities and relationships, choosing keys, normalizing tables, and using constraints and indexes sensibly. Once learned, you can turn requirements into a clean, consistent database schema.

documents.title: NoSQL databases
documents.text: NoSQL databases. Also known as: non-relational databases, document databases, mongodb, key-value stores, nosql, redis, cassandra. Covers non-relational data stores such as document, key-value, wide-column and graph databases, and when to choose them over relational ones. A learner can model data for a NoSQL store, run basic queries, and weigh consistency and scaling trade-offs.

documents.title: Git version control
documents.text: Git version control. Also known as: git, version control, source control, git commands, github basics, git branching. Tracking changes to files with Git: committing, branching, merging, resolving conflicts and syncing with remote repositories. Once learned, you can collaborate on code safely and recover from mistakes in a project's history.

documents.title: Linux command line
documents.text: Linux command line. Also known as: bash, shell, terminal, unix shell, cli, bash scripting, command prompt basics. Working in a Linux shell: navigating the filesystem, managing files and permissions, using pipes and redirection, and running and scripting basic commands. Once learned, you can operate a Linux machine and automate simple tasks from the terminal.

documents.title: HTML and CSS
documents.text: HTML and CSS. Also known as: html, css, html5, css3, web page markup, web styling, front-end basics, stylesheets. Covers structuring web pages with semantic HTML and styling them with CSS, including the box model, flexbox, grid and responsive layout. Once learned, you can build and style a responsive static web page from scratch.

documents.title: Web accessibility
documents.text: Web accessibility. Also known as: a11y, wcag, accessible web design, aria, inclusive web design, screen reader accessibility. Web accessibility is the part of HTML and CSS work focused on making sites usable by people with disabilities. Once you know it, you can apply WCAG guidelines, semantic markup, ARIA, keyboard support and contrast rules, and audit pages with assistive tech.

documents.title: React
documents.text: React. Also known as: reactjs, react.js, react js, jsx, react components, react framework. React is a part of JavaScript's UI ecosystem: building user interfaces from reusable components, JSX, props, state and rendering. Once learned, you can build and structure interactive single-page front-end apps.

documents.title: React hooks
documents.text: React hooks. Also known as: hooks, useState, useEffect, custom hooks, react state hooks, useContext. The hooks API for function components in React: managing state, side effects, context, refs and memoization, and writing custom hooks. Once you know it, you can build and debug stateful function components without classes.

documents.title: Next.js
documents.text: Next.js. Also known as: next, next js, nextjs framework, react server components, app router, vercel next. Next.js is a framework built on React for production web apps, covering file-based routing, server and client rendering, data fetching, and deployment. Once learned, you can build and ship full-stack React sites with server-side rendering and API routes.

documents.title: Node.js
documents.text: Node.js. Also known as: node, node js, server-side javascript, npm, express. Node.js is the JavaScript runtime for running code outside the browser. It covers modules, the event loop, file and network I/O, npm packages, and building simple command-line tools and web servers; learners can build backend services.

documents.title: REST API design
documents.text: REST API design. Also known as: RESTful API design, REST APIs, web API design, RESTful services, designing HTTP APIs, API design. How to design clean, consistent web APIs around resources, HTTP methods, status codes, versioning, pagination and error handling. Once learned, you can design and document a RESTful API that other developers can use easily.

documents.title: GraphQL
documents.text: GraphQL. Also known as: graph ql, gql, graphql api, graphql queries, apollo graphql. A query language and runtime for APIs where clients request exactly the data they need. Covers schemas, types, queries, mutations, resolvers and subscriptions, so you can design and consume a GraphQL API.

documents.title: Data structures
documents.text: Data structures. Also known as: data structure, dsa, arrays and linked lists, stacks and queues, hash tables, trees and heaps. Covers the core ways of organising data in memory: arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, trees, heaps and graphs. Once learned, you can choose a suitable structure for a problem and reason about its time and space trade-offs.

documents.title: Algorithms
documents.text: Algorithms. Also known as: algorithm design, algorithm analysis, big o notation, sorting and searching, algos, algorithmic thinking. Designing and analysing step-by-step procedures for solving problems efficiently, including sorting, searching, recursion, dynamic programming and complexity analysis. Once learned, you can choose and implement suitable algorithms and reason about their running time.

documents.title: Object-oriented programming
documents.text: Object-oriented programming. Also known as: OOP, object oriented programming, object-oriented design, classes and objects, encapsulation and inheritance, object-oriented paradigm. Covers modelling software with classes and objects, including encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction. Once learned, you can design and build programs as collaborating objects and judge when an object-oriented approach fits.

documents.title: Functional programming
documents.text: Functional programming. Also known as: FP, pure functions, functional paradigm, immutability, higher-order functions, functional style. A programming paradigm built on pure functions, immutable data, and composition. Once you know it, you can use map/filter/reduce, closures, and higher-order functions to write predictable code with fewer side effects.

documents.title: Software design patterns
documents.text: Software design patterns. Also known as: gang of four patterns, GoF patterns, software patterns, creational structural behavioral patterns, singleton factory observer, oop design patterns. Reusable solutions to common software design problems, such as factory, observer, strategy and decorator. Once you know them, you can recognise recurring problems in a codebase, choose a fitting pattern and apply it without overengineering.

documents.title: Clean code and refactoring
documents.text: Clean code and refactoring. Also known as: clean code, refactoring, code smells, code readability, code quality, technical debt cleanup, readable code. Writing code that is readable and easy to change, and improving existing code safely without altering its behavior. Covers naming, small functions, removing duplication, spotting code smells, and applying common refactoring moves.

documents.title: Software testing
documents.text: Software testing. Also known as: QA, quality assurance, unit testing, automated testing, test automation, software QA. Covers the principles and practice of verifying that software works: unit, integration and end-to-end tests, test design, mocking, and coverage. After learning it, you can write reliable automated tests and judge what and how much to test.

documents.title: Test-driven development
documents.text: Test-driven development. Also known as: TDD, red green refactor, test-first development, test first programming. The practice of writing a failing automated test before the code, then making it pass and refactoring in small cycles. It narrows software testing to a design workflow; learners can build features incrementally with a reliable test suite.

documents.title: Regular expressions
documents.text: Regular expressions. Also known as: regex, regexp, regex patterns, pattern matching, grep patterns. Writing and reading patterns that match, extract and replace text, including character classes, quantifiers, groups, anchors and lookarounds. Once learned, you can validate input, search logs and transform text in code or editors.

documents.title: pandas (Python data analysis)
documents.text: pandas (Python data analysis). Also known as: pandas library, python pandas, dataframes, dataframe, pd.DataFrame, python data analysis. The pandas library for Python, covering Series and DataFrames, loading data, cleaning, filtering, grouping, merging and summarizing tabular data. Once learned, you can analyze and reshape real-world datasets in Python; this narrows Python to data analysis.

documents.title: Docker
documents.text: Docker. Also known as: containers, containerization, dockerfile, docker compose, docker containers, docker images. Packaging applications and their dependencies into containers using images, Dockerfiles, volumes, networks and Compose. Once learned, you can build, run and share containerized apps on a single machine and debug common container issues.

documents.title: Kubernetes
documents.text: Kubernetes. Also known as: k8s, kube, kubectl, container orchestration, k8s clusters. Covers running and managing containerized applications on a cluster: pods, deployments, services, configuration, scaling and rolling updates. Once learned, you can deploy, expose and troubleshoot an application using kubectl and YAML manifests.

documents.title: CI/CD pipelines
documents.text: CI/CD pipelines. Also known as: continuous integration, continuous delivery, continuous deployment, build pipeline, deployment pipeline, github actions, jenkins, devops pipelines. Covers automating the build, test and release of software with pipelines that run on every change. Once learned, you can set up a pipeline that tests code, builds artifacts and deploys them safely, including basic rollback and secrets handling.

documents.title: Infrastructure as code
documents.text: Infrastructure as code. Also known as: iac, terraform, infrastructure automation, cloudformation, declarative infrastructure, pulumi. Defining and managing servers, networks and cloud resources through version-controlled code instead of manual setup. Once learned, you can write, review and apply reproducible infrastructure configurations and manage changes safely.

documents.title: Cloud computing fundamentals
documents.text: Cloud computing fundamentals. Also known as: cloud basics, intro to cloud, cloud computing, iaas paas saas, cloud concepts, cloud services overview. Core ideas behind cloud computing: service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), deployment models, virtualization, elasticity, shared responsibility and pricing. Once learned, you can explain how cloud platforms work and choose suitable services for basic workloads.

documents.title: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
documents.text: Amazon Web Services (AWS). Also known as: amazon web services, aws cloud, ec2 and s3, amazon cloud, aws services. The AWS cloud platform in particular, a specific application of cloud computing fundamentals. Covers core services such as compute, storage, networking, databases and IAM, so you can design, deploy and secure basic applications on AWS.

documents.title: Observability and monitoring
documents.text: Observability and monitoring. Also known as: monitoring and logging, metrics logs and traces, application monitoring, apm, site reliability monitoring, telemetry. Covers instrumenting software with metrics, logs and traces, building dashboards and alerts, and using them to detect, diagnose and understand problems in running systems. Learners can set up basic monitoring and investigate incidents.

documents.title: Computer networking
documents.text: Computer networking. Also known as: networking basics, network fundamentals, tcp/ip, osi model, ip addressing, lan and wan, networks. Covers how computers communicate over networks: the layered models, IP addressing and subnets, TCP and UDP, DNS, routing, and common network devices. Once learned, you can explain how data travels between machines and troubleshoot basic connectivity problems.

documents.title: HTTP
documents.text: HTTP. Also known as: hypertext transfer protocol, http methods, http status codes, http headers, https, http requests. The application-layer protocol of the web, a part of computer networking: requests and responses, methods, status codes, headers, caching, cookies and HTTPS. Once learned, you can inspect, debug and reason about web traffic between clients and servers.

documents.title: Web application security
documents.text: Web application security. Also known as: application security, appsec, owasp top 10, xss and csrf, secure web development, web app security. Covers how web applications are attacked and defended, including injection, cross-site scripting, CSRF, and insecure configuration. Once learned, you can spot common vulnerabilities and apply standard defenses in a web app.

documents.title: Authentication and authorization
documents.text: Authentication and authorization. Also known as: authn and authz, authn, authz, login and access control, user authentication, oauth, access control, identity and access management. A part of web application security covering how systems verify who a user is and decide what they may do: password storage, sessions, tokens, OAuth and role-based access. Learners can design and implement secure login and permission checks.

documents.title: Operating systems
documents.text: Operating systems. Also known as: OS fundamentals, OS concepts, kernel basics, process scheduling and memory management, operating system internals. How operating systems manage processes, memory, file systems and devices on top of hardware. Once learned, you can explain scheduling, virtual memory and system calls, and reason about how programs interact with the OS.

documents.title: Concurrency and parallelism
documents.text: Concurrency and parallelism. Also known as: multithreading, threads and locks, parallel programming, concurrent programming, race conditions, multiprocessing. How programs run multiple tasks at once, covering threads, processes, locks, race conditions, deadlocks and common concurrency models. Once learned, you can design and debug code that safely shares work across cores or tasks.

documents.title: System design
documents.text: System design. Also known as: software architecture design, distributed systems design, scalable system design, high-level design, architecture design interview, designing large-scale systems. Designing scalable, reliable software systems by choosing components such as databases, caches, queues and load balancers and weighing trade-offs. A learner can sketch and justify an architecture for a real product's requirements.

documents.title: Microservices architecture
documents.text: Microservices architecture. Also known as: microservice architecture, microservices pattern, service-oriented architecture, distributed services, service decomposition, monolith to microservices. Microservices is a part of system design focused on splitting an application into small, independently deployable services. Once learned, you can decide service boundaries, design inter-service communication, and handle data consistency and failures.

documents.title: Compilers and interpreters
documents.text: Compilers and interpreters. Also known as: compiler design, compiler construction, interpreter design, parsing and lexing, language implementation, programming language implementation. How source code is turned into running programs: lexing, parsing, syntax trees, semantic analysis, code generation, and interpretation. Once learned, you can build a simple interpreter or compiler and reason about how language features are implemented.

documents.title: Mobile app development
documents.text: Mobile app development. Also known as: app development, building mobile apps, ios and android development, android development, ios development, cross-platform apps, react native, flutter. Designing, building and shipping apps for phones and tablets, covering app structure, screens and navigation, device features, local and remote data, and release to app stores. Once learned, you can build a simple working app for iOS or Android.

documents.title: LLM application development
documents.text: LLM application development. Also known as: building llm apps, llm apps, generative ai development, rag, prompt engineering, ai app development, openai api, langchain. Building software that uses large language models through APIs: prompt design, structured outputs, retrieval-augmented generation, tool calling, and evaluation. Once learned, you can design, ship and test a working LLM-powered feature or app.

documents.title: Algebra
documents.text: Algebra. Also known as: elementary algebra, college algebra, algebra 1, algebra 2, solving equations, algebraic expressions, intro algebra. Covers working with variables and expressions, solving linear and quadratic equations and inequalities, factoring, exponents, and systems of equations. Once learned, you can model simple problems symbolically and solve for unknowns.

documents.title: Functions and graphs
documents.text: Functions and graphs. Also known as: function graphing, graphing functions, function notation, precalculus functions, domain and range, function transformations. A part of algebra focused on functions: notation, domain and range, graphing, transformations, composition and inverses, and the main families (linear, quadratic, polynomial, exponential, logarithmic). Learners can read, sketch and interpret graphs and model relationships with functions.

documents.title: Geometry
documents.text: Geometry. Also known as: euclidean geometry, plane geometry, geometry basics, shapes and angles, solid geometry. Covers the properties of points, lines, angles, triangles, circles, polygons and solids, including area, volume, congruence, similarity and basic proofs. Once learned, you can solve measurement problems and reason about spatial relationships.

documents.title: Trigonometry
documents.text: Trigonometry. Also known as: trig, sine and cosine, trigonometric functions, sin cos tan, unit circle, right triangle trigonometry. The study of angles and the relationships between side lengths in triangles, extended to periodic functions via the unit circle. Once learned, you can solve triangles, use radians, apply trig identities and model waves and rotations.

documents.title: Calculus
documents.text: Calculus. Also known as: calc, infinitesimal calculus, differentiation and integration, derivatives and integrals, single-variable calculus. The study of change and accumulation through limits, derivatives and integrals. Once learned, you can analyse rates of change, find optima and areas, and apply these ideas to science, engineering and economics problems.

documents.title: Differential calculus
documents.text: Differential calculus. Also known as: derivatives, differentiation, calculus 1, limits and derivatives, rates of change, diff calc. The part of calculus about limits, derivatives and rates of change. A learner can differentiate common functions, apply the chain rule, and use derivatives for tangent lines, optimization and curve sketching.

documents.title: Integral calculus
documents.text: Integral calculus. Also known as: integration, integrals, antiderivatives, definite integrals, integration techniques, calculus 2. The part of calculus about accumulation: antiderivatives, definite integrals, the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, and integration techniques. Once learned, you can compute areas, volumes and totals from rates of change.

documents.title: Multivariable calculus
documents.text: Multivariable calculus. Also known as: multivariate calculus, calc 3, calculus 3, vector calculus, partial derivatives, calculus of several variables. Extends calculus to functions of several variables: partial derivatives, gradients, multiple integrals, and line and surface integrals. A learner can optimize multivariable functions and compute volumes, flux, and work in 2D and 3D.

documents.title: Differential equations
documents.text: Differential equations. Also known as: diff eq, ODEs, ordinary differential equations, DEs, PDEs basics, modeling with differential equations. Covers equations relating a function to its derivatives, including first-order and second-order ordinary differential equations, solution methods, and modeling change over time. Learners can set up and solve common ODEs and interpret their solutions.

documents.title: Linear algebra
documents.text: Linear algebra. Also known as: matrix algebra, matrices and vectors, vector spaces, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, matrix theory. Covers vectors, matrices, systems of linear equations, vector spaces, linear transformations, determinants, and eigenvalues. Once learned, you can solve linear systems, interpret matrices as transformations, and apply them in data science and engineering.

documents.title: Discrete mathematics
documents.text: Discrete mathematics. Also known as: discrete math, discrete structures, combinatorics and logic, propositional logic, set theory and proofs, counting and proofs. Covers the math of countable structures: logic, sets, proofs, induction, relations, counting and recurrences. Once learned, you can reason rigorously, write simple proofs and count arrangements, which supports computer science work.

documents.title: Graph theory
documents.text: Graph theory. Also known as: graphs and networks, network theory, graph algorithms, vertices and edges, trees and graphs. The mathematics of graphs: vertices and edges, paths, cycles, connectivity, trees, coloring, and matching. A learner can model problems as graphs and prove or apply basic results about them. It narrows discrete mathematics to its graph-focused part.

documents.title: Numerical methods
documents.text: Numerical methods. Also known as: numerical analysis, scientific computing, numerical computation, numerical algorithms, root finding, numerical integration. Covers algorithms for approximating solutions to mathematical problems on a computer, including root finding, interpolation, numerical integration and differentiation, and solving linear systems, along with error and stability. Learners can choose and implement suitable methods and judge their accuracy.

documents.title: Mathematical optimization
documents.text: Mathematical optimization. Also known as: optimization, optimisation, linear programming, convex optimization, operations research, constrained optimization, gradient descent. Covers formulating problems as objectives and constraints and solving them: unconstrained and constrained optimization, Lagrange multipliers, linear programming, convexity, and gradient-based methods. Learners can model and solve basic optimization problems.

documents.title: Probability
documents.text: Probability. Also known as: probability theory, chance and likelihood, random variables, conditional probability, probability distributions, stochastic basics. Covers how to quantify uncertainty: counting methods, conditional probability, independence, random variables, common distributions, and expected value. Once learned, you can model random events and compute likelihoods of outcomes.

documents.title: Statistics
documents.text: Statistics. Also known as: stats, descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, statistical analysis, data analysis basics, statistical inference. Covers describing data with summaries and charts, sampling, distributions, confidence intervals and the logic of drawing conclusions from samples. Once learned, you can interpret quantitative results and choose sensible basic methods for analysing data.

documents.title: Hypothesis testing
documents.text: Hypothesis testing. Also known as: significance testing, null hypothesis testing, p-values, t-test, statistical significance, NHST, A/B test analysis. The part of statistics that uses sample data to decide whether an observed effect is likely real or due to chance, covering null and alternative hypotheses, p-values, errors and common tests. Once learned, you can pick, run and interpret a test such as a t-test or chi-square.

documents.title: Regression analysis
documents.text: Regression analysis. Also known as: linear regression, regression modeling, least squares, OLS, logistic regression, regression models. A part of statistics focused on modeling the relationship between a response and one or more predictors. Once learned, you can fit and interpret linear and logistic regression models, check their assumptions, and use them to explain and predict.

documents.title: Bayesian statistics
documents.text: Bayesian statistics. Also known as: bayesian inference, bayes theorem, bayesian analysis, posterior probability, bayesian modeling, mcmc. A part of statistics that treats unknown quantities as probability distributions and updates beliefs with data using Bayes' theorem. Once learned, you can specify priors, compute posteriors, and interpret credible intervals and simple Bayesian models.

documents.title: Machine learning
documents.text: Machine learning. Also known as: ML, statistical learning, predictive modeling, supervised learning, scikit-learn, applied machine learning. Covers how to build models that learn patterns from data: supervised and unsupervised methods, training, evaluation, overfitting and feature engineering. Once learned, you can frame a prediction problem, train and validate a model, and interpret its results.

documents.title: Deep learning
documents.text: Deep learning. Also known as: neural networks, deep neural networks, DNN, neural nets, CNN, transformers, backpropagation. Deep learning is the part of machine learning that trains multi-layer neural networks, covering backpropagation, convolutional and sequence models, and transformers. Once learned, you can build, train and tune neural networks for tasks like images and text.

documents.title: Classical mechanics
documents.text: Classical mechanics. Also known as: newtonian mechanics, newton's laws, physics 101, kinematics and dynamics, intro physics mechanics, mechanics. Covers motion and forces: kinematics, Newton's laws, work and energy, momentum, rotation, and gravity. Once learned, you can model and solve problems about moving objects, collisions, and simple oscillating systems.

documents.title: Electricity and magnetism
documents.text: Electricity and magnetism. Also known as: electromagnetism, e&m, electromagnetic theory, maxwell's equations, electrostatics, physics 2. Covers electric charge, fields, potential, currents, magnetic fields, induction and Maxwell's equations at an introductory level. After learning it, you can analyse charge distributions, field forces and simple electromagnetic induction problems.

documents.title: Thermodynamics
documents.text: Thermodynamics. Also known as: heat and thermodynamics, laws of thermodynamics, entropy and heat, heat engines, statistical thermodynamics basics, thermal physics. Covers temperature, heat, work, internal energy, the laws of thermodynamics, entropy, and ideal gases and heat engines. Once learned, you can analyse energy transfers and efficiency in thermal systems and cycles.

documents.title: Waves and optics
documents.text: Waves and optics. Also known as: wave physics, physical optics, geometrical optics, light and sound waves, wave motion, optics. Covers oscillations, wave propagation, sound, superposition, interference, diffraction, and light behaviour including reflection, refraction, lenses and mirrors. Learners can analyse wave phenomena and solve basic optical systems problems.

documents.title: Special relativity
documents.text: Special relativity. Also known as: special theory of relativity, einstein's relativity, lorentz transformations, time dilation, length contraction, spacetime physics. Covers Einstein's 1905 theory of motion at speeds near light: relativity of simultaneity, time dilation, length contraction, Lorentz transformations and mass-energy equivalence. Learners can solve problems comparing observers in different inertial frames.

documents.title: Quantum mechanics
documents.text: Quantum mechanics. Also known as: quantum physics, quantum theory, qm, wave mechanics, schrödinger equation, wave function. The physics of matter and energy at atomic and subatomic scales, covering wavefunctions, the Schrödinger equation, quantization, spin and measurement. A learner can solve basic problems such as particle in a box, the harmonic oscillator and the hydrogen atom.

documents.title: Astronomy
documents.text: Astronomy. Also known as: astrophysics, space science, stargazing, cosmology, planets and stars, celestial objects. Covers the night sky, the solar system, stars and their life cycles, galaxies and the large-scale universe. Once learned, you can explain how celestial objects move and form, interpret basic observations, and read popular astronomy with understanding.

documents.title: General chemistry
documents.text: General chemistry. Also known as: gen chem, intro chemistry, introductory chemistry, chemistry 101, basic chemistry, college chemistry. Covers atoms, the periodic table, bonding, stoichiometry, states of matter, solutions, acids and bases, and basic energy changes. Once learned, you can balance equations, do mole calculations, and explain why substances react and behave as they do.

documents.title: Chemical equilibrium and kinetics
documents.text: Chemical equilibrium and kinetics. Also known as: reaction kinetics, chemical kinetics, le chatelier's principle, equilibrium constant, reaction rates, rate laws. A part of general chemistry covering how fast reactions occur and how reversible reactions reach balance. Learners can write rate laws and equilibrium expressions, use K and Q, and predict how conditions shift a reaction.

documents.title: Organic chemistry
documents.text: Organic chemistry. Also known as: orgo, orgo chem, organic chem, carbon chemistry, organic reaction mechanisms. The study of carbon-based compounds: functional groups, structure and stereochemistry, and the reaction mechanisms that connect them. Once learned, you can name organic molecules, predict reaction products, and propose simple synthesis routes.

documents.title: Biochemistry
documents.text: Biochemistry. Also known as: biological chemistry, biochem, chemistry of life, metabolism and enzymes, physiological chemistry. The chemistry of living systems: structure and function of proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids, enzyme kinetics, and core metabolic pathways. Learners can explain how cells extract and use energy and how molecules drive biological processes.

documents.title: Cell biology
documents.text: Cell biology. Also known as: cytology, cell structure and function, cell biology basics, organelles, cell cycle and division. Covers the structure and function of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells: organelles, membranes, transport, energy use, signaling and the cell cycle. Once learned, you can explain how cells work and interpret basic cell-level experiments.

documents.title: Genetics
documents.text: Genetics. Also known as: heredity, mendelian genetics, inheritance, genes and heredity, classical genetics, population genetics. Covers how traits are inherited and how genes vary: Mendelian patterns, chromosomes, linkage, pedigrees, mutations and basic population genetics. Once learned, you can predict inheritance outcomes and interpret simple genetic data.

documents.title: Molecular biology
documents.text: Molecular biology. Also known as: molecular biology of the gene, dna replication and transcription, gene expression, central dogma, pcr and cloning, molecular genetics. How cells store, copy, read and regulate genetic information at the molecular level: DNA replication, transcription, translation, gene regulation and core lab techniques like PCR and cloning. Learners can explain and interpret these processes and experiments.

documents.title: Evolutionary biology
documents.text: Evolutionary biology. Also known as: evolution, natural selection, darwinian evolution, evolutionary theory, phylogenetics, common descent, speciation. Covers how populations change over time through natural selection, drift, mutation and gene flow, and how species arise and are related. Once learned, you can explain adaptation, read phylogenetic trees and evaluate evidence for evolutionary claims.

documents.title: Ecology
documents.text: Ecology. Also known as: ecosystems, population ecology, community ecology, environmental biology, food webs, ecological science. The study of how organisms interact with each other and their environments, covering populations, communities, ecosystems, energy flow and nutrient cycles. Once learned, you can interpret ecological data and explain how ecosystems function and respond to change.

documents.title: Microbiology
documents.text: Microbiology. Also known as: microbes, bacteriology, microbial biology, medical microbiology, virology, microorganisms. The study of microscopic organisms such as bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoa: their structure, growth, metabolism, genetics and roles in health, disease and the environment. Once learned, you can explain how microbes live and cause infection and how they are controlled.

documents.title: Human anatomy and physiology
documents.text: Human anatomy and physiology. Also known as: anatomy and physiology, a&p, human body systems, human biology, anatomy, physiology. Covers the structure and function of the major human body systems, from musculoskeletal and cardiovascular to nervous and endocrine, and how they work together to maintain homeostasis. Learners can explain how organs and systems function and relate them to health.

documents.title: Neuroscience
documents.text: Neuroscience. Also known as: neurobiology, brain science, neural science, neurophysiology, cognitive neuroscience, how the brain works. Covers the structure and function of the nervous system: neurons, synapses, electrical signaling, major brain regions, and how they underlie sensation, movement, learning and behavior. Learners can explain how neural circuits work and read introductory research findings.

documents.title: Epidemiology
documents.text: Epidemiology. Also known as: disease epidemiology, public health epidemiology, outbreak investigation, disease surveillance, epi, study of disease patterns. The study of how diseases and health outcomes are distributed in populations and what causes them. Covers measures of disease frequency, study designs, bias and confounding, and outbreak investigation, so a learner can interpret and critique health studies.

documents.title: Geology
documents.text: Geology. Also known as: geology basics, earth science, physical geology, plate tectonics, rocks and minerals, geoscience. Covers how the Earth is built and how it changes: minerals, rock types, plate tectonics, volcanoes, earthquakes, weathering and geologic time. Once learned, you can read a geologic map, identify common rocks, and explain how landscapes formed.

documents.title: Climate science
documents.text: Climate science. Also known as: climatology, global warming science, climate change science, atmospheric science, earth's climate system. Covers how Earth's climate system works, including the greenhouse effect, energy balance, carbon cycle, and evidence for past and present climate change. Learners can interpret climate data and explain causes, feedbacks, and projected impacts.

documents.title: Electrical circuits
documents.text: Electrical circuits. Also known as: circuit analysis, circuit theory, dc circuits, ohm's law, kirchhoff's laws, basic electronics. Covers voltage, current, resistance, power and the laws (Ohm, Kirchhoff) used to analyze resistive, capacitive and inductive circuits. Once learned, you can analyze and design simple DC and basic AC circuits and predict their behavior.

documents.title: Digital logic design
documents.text: Digital logic design. Also known as: digital design, logic design, boolean logic circuits, logic gates, combinational and sequential logic, digital electronics. Covers Boolean algebra, logic gates, combinational circuits, flip-flops, registers, counters and simple state machines. A learner can design, simplify and analyze basic digital circuits such as adders, multiplexers and sequential controllers.

documents.title: Signals and systems
documents.text: Signals and systems. Also known as: signal processing basics, LTI systems, convolution and Fourier transforms, linear time-invariant systems, Fourier analysis, signals and linear systems. Covers how signals are represented and how linear time-invariant systems act on them, including convolution, Fourier and Laplace transforms, and frequency response. Once learned, you can analyze and predict how a system filters or transforms a signal.

documents.title: Control systems
documents.text: Control systems. Also known as: control theory, feedback control, PID control, classical control, automatic control, feedback systems. Covers how feedback is used to make dynamic systems behave as desired: modelling with transfer functions, stability analysis, and designing controllers such as PID. Once learned, you can analyse a system's response and tune a basic feedback controller.

documents.title: Engineering mechanics (statics)
documents.text: Engineering mechanics (statics). Also known as: statics, engineering statics, static equilibrium, free body diagrams, structural mechanics basics, applied mechanics. Covers forces, moments, and equilibrium of rigid bodies at rest, including free-body diagrams, trusses, frames, friction, and centroids. Once learned, you can analyze the forces in simple structures and machines.

documents.title: Fluid mechanics
documents.text: Fluid mechanics. Also known as: fluid dynamics, hydraulics, fluid flow, bernoulli equation, hydrostatics, navier-stokes. The study of how liquids and gases behave at rest and in motion, covering pressure, buoyancy, continuity, Bernoulli's equation, viscosity and pipe flow. Once learned, you can analyse flow in pipes, forces on submerged bodies and basic fluid systems.

documents.title: Materials science
documents.text: Materials science. Also known as: materials engineering, engineering materials, materials science and engineering, material properties, metallurgy basics, polymers and ceramics. Covers how the atomic structure and processing of metals, ceramics, polymers and composites determine their mechanical, thermal and electrical properties. A learner can explain why materials behave as they do and choose suitable materials for a design need.

documents.title: Public speaking
documents.text: Public speaking. Also known as: presentation skills, speechmaking, oratory, giving speeches, presenting to an audience, stage presence. Planning, structuring and delivering talks to live or virtual audiences. Once you know it, you can prepare a clear speech, manage nerves, use voice and body language well, and adapt your message to different audiences.

documents.title: Business writing
documents.text: Business writing. Also known as: professional writing, workplace writing, business communication writing, writing emails and reports, corporate writing. Clear, concise written communication for the workplace: emails, memos, reports and proposals. Once you know it, you can structure a message for its audience and purpose, edit for clarity and tone, and get readers to act.

documents.title: Storytelling
documents.text: Storytelling. Also known as: narrative craft, story structure, narrative technique, telling stories, story arc, narrative storytelling. The craft of shaping events, characters and tension into a compelling narrative for an audience, in speech or writing. Once learned, you can structure a story with a clear arc and use it to engage, persuade or explain.

documents.title: Creative writing
documents.text: Creative writing. Also known as: fiction writing, writing fiction, short story writing, narrative writing, poetry writing, novel writing, creative composition. Covers the craft of writing original fiction, poetry and personal prose, including character, voice, scene, imagery and revision. A learner can draft and polish short stories or poems and give their work a distinct style.

documents.title: Copywriting
documents.text: Copywriting. Also known as: ad copy, sales copy, persuasive writing, direct response copywriting, advertising copy, marketing copy. Writing persuasive text for ads, landing pages, emails and product pages that gets readers to act. Once learned, you can write headlines, benefit-led copy and calls to action, and tailor the message to an audience and goal.

documents.title: English grammar and usage
documents.text: English grammar and usage. Also known as: grammar, english usage, english syntax, parts of speech, sentence structure, punctuation and grammar, english language rules. The rules of English words, sentences, punctuation and usage. Once learned, you can build clear grammatical sentences, fix common errors, and choose correct forms in writing and speech.

documents.title: Spanish
documents.text: Spanish. Also known as: spanish language, español, castellano, learn spanish, spanish for beginners, conversational spanish. Learning Spanish as a second language: pronunciation, core vocabulary, verb conjugation and sentence structure. Once learned, you can understand and hold everyday conversations and read and write simple texts in Spanish.

documents.title: Negotiation
documents.text: Negotiation. Also known as: negotiating, negotiation skills, bargaining, deal making, principled negotiation, salary negotiation. Preparing for and conducting negotiations: identifying interests, alternatives and bargaining ranges, making and answering offers, and reaching agreements that hold up. Once learned, you can plan and run a negotiation in work or business settings.

documents.title: Sales
documents.text: Sales. Also known as: selling, sales techniques, prospecting, closing deals, b2b sales, sales skills. The process of finding, qualifying and persuading potential buyers and closing deals. Once you know it, you can run a sales conversation from discovery through objection handling to close and manage a basic pipeline.

documents.title: Customer service
documents.text: Customer service. Also known as: customer support, customer care, client service, customer experience, help desk support, customer success. Serving customers well across phone, email and chat: listening, handling questions and complaints, and recovering from problems. Once learned, you can resolve issues professionally and leave customers satisfied.

documents.title: Project management
documents.text: Project management. Also known as: managing projects, project planning, project delivery, pm, project scheduling, project coordination. Covers how to define project scope, plan schedules, budgets and resources, manage risks and stakeholders, and track delivery to completion. Once learned, you can plan and run a small to mid-sized project from kickoff to close.

documents.title: Agile and Scrum
documents.text: Agile and Scrum. Also known as: scrum, agile, agile methodology, sprints, scrum master, kanban and scrum. Agile and Scrum is the part of project management focused on iterative delivery: sprints, backlogs, standups, reviews and retrospectives. Once learned, you can run or take part in a Scrum team and adapt its practices to changing requirements.

documents.title: Product management
documents.text: Product management. Also known as: product manager, PM, product ownership, product strategy and roadmapping, product development management, product owner. Covers how to decide what a product should do and why: discovering customer problems, prioritising work, writing requirements, building roadmaps and working with engineering and design to ship. You can run a basic product cycle from idea to launch.

documents.title: User research
documents.text: User research. Also known as: ux research, customer research, user interviews, usability testing, design research, customer discovery. Covers planning and running studies such as interviews, surveys, and usability tests to understand user needs and behaviors. A learner can choose suitable methods, gather evidence, and turn findings into insights that guide product and design decisions.

documents.title: UX design
documents.text: UX design. Also known as: user experience design, UX, interaction design, usability design, product design, wireframing, user interface design. Designing digital products that are usable, useful and pleasant, from user flows and wireframes to prototypes and usability testing. A learner can structure an interface around user needs and iterate on a design based on feedback.

documents.title: Graphic design fundamentals
documents.text: Graphic design fundamentals. Also known as: graphic design, design principles, visual design, design basics, typography and layout, color theory and layout. Core principles of visual design: layout, hierarchy, typography, color, contrast, and composition. Once learned, you can create clear, balanced designs such as posters, social graphics, and slides, and critique design choices.

documents.title: Photography
documents.text: Photography. Also known as: digital photography, camera basics, exposure triangle, photo composition, taking photos, dslr photography. Covers how to use a camera to make deliberate images: exposure (aperture, shutter speed, ISO), focus, light, composition, and basic editing. Once learned, you can shoot well-exposed, well-composed photos in varied conditions and develop a personal style.

documents.title: Drawing
documents.text: Drawing. Also known as: sketching, pencil drawing, figure drawing, drawing basics, observational drawing, learn to draw. Covers the core skills of representational drawing: line control, shape and proportion, perspective, shading and value, and drawing from observation. Once learned, you can sketch objects, scenes and figures with believable form and depth.

documents.title: Music theory
documents.text: Music theory. Also known as: music fundamentals, music notation, scales and chords, harmony, reading sheet music, music basics. The language of Western music: notation, rhythm, scales, keys, intervals, chords and basic harmony. Once learned, you can read simple scores, analyse how songs are built, and use that knowledge to write or arrange music.

documents.title: Digital marketing
documents.text: Digital marketing. Also known as: online marketing, internet marketing, e-marketing, social media marketing, email marketing, performance marketing. Covers promoting products and services through online channels such as search, social media, email and paid ads. Once learned, you can plan a basic multichannel campaign, set goals, track results and adjust spending based on the data.

documents.title: Search engine optimization (SEO)
documents.text: Search engine optimization (SEO). Also known as: search engine optimisation, organic search, on-page seo, technical seo, keyword research, link building, google ranking. The part of digital marketing focused on earning organic search traffic. Covers keyword research, on-page and technical optimization, content and link building, so you can audit a site and plan improvements that raise its search rankings.

documents.title: Entrepreneurship
documents.text: Entrepreneurship. Also known as: startups, starting a business, startup founding, new venture creation, business startup, founder skills. Covers how to find and validate a business idea, build a basic business model, launch and fund a new venture, and find early customers. Once learned, you can take an idea to a tested first version of a small business or startup.

documents.title: Business strategy
documents.text: Business strategy. Also known as: corporate strategy, competitive strategy, strategic management, strategic planning, competitive advantage, business planning. How organizations choose where to compete and how to win: analyzing industries and competitors, identifying sources of competitive advantage, and shaping positioning and growth choices. Learners can evaluate a company's strategy and propose strategic options.

documents.title: Business law basics
documents.text: Business law basics. Also known as: commercial law, corporate law basics, contract law, legal basics for business, business legal essentials. Covers the core legal concepts behind running a business: contracts, business structures, liability, intellectual property, employment basics and regulatory compliance. Learners can spot common legal risks and know when to seek a lawyer.

documents.title: Accounting fundamentals
documents.text: Accounting fundamentals. Also known as: bookkeeping, accounting basics, financial accounting, double-entry bookkeeping, debits and credits, intro to accounting. Covers how businesses record and summarize financial activity: double-entry bookkeeping, the accounting equation, journals and ledgers, and preparing basic financial statements. Once learned, you can record transactions and produce a simple balance sheet and income statement.

documents.title: Financial statement analysis
documents.text: Financial statement analysis. Also known as: financial analysis, reading financial statements, ratio analysis, fundamental analysis, analyzing balance sheets and income statements. Interpreting a company's income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement using ratios and trend analysis. Once learned, you can judge profitability, liquidity, leverage and cash generation and compare firms.

documents.title: Corporate finance
documents.text: Corporate finance. Also known as: managerial finance, business finance, capital budgeting, corporate financial management, valuation and capital structure, finance for business. How companies make financial decisions: evaluating investments with NPV and IRR, estimating cost of capital, choosing between debt and equity, and managing working capital. Learners can value projects and judge a firm's financing choices.

documents.title: Personal finance
documents.text: Personal finance. Also known as: money management, personal money management, budgeting, household finance, managing money, financial planning. Covers managing your own money: budgeting, saving, debt and credit, taxes, insurance, and setting up retirement and emergency funds. Once learned, you can build a budget and a realistic plan for your financial goals.

documents.title: Investing fundamentals
documents.text: Investing fundamentals. Also known as: investing basics, stock market basics, investing for beginners, stocks and bonds, index fund investing, portfolio basics. A part of personal finance focused on growing money through assets such as stocks, bonds and funds. Covers risk, return, diversification and fees, so a learner can build and maintain a simple diversified portfolio.

documents.title: Microeconomics
documents.text: Microeconomics. Also known as: micro, micro economics, price theory, supply and demand, consumer and firm behavior. How individuals, households and firms make choices under scarcity and how markets set prices and quantities. Covers supply and demand, elasticity, costs, market structures and market failures, so you can analyze everyday and business decisions.

documents.title: Macroeconomics
documents.text: Macroeconomics. Also known as: macro, macro economics, national economics, aggregate economics, economy-wide economics, gdp and inflation. The study of whole economies: GDP, inflation, unemployment, interest rates, fiscal and monetary policy, and international trade. Once learned, you can interpret economic news and explain how policy choices and shocks affect growth and prices.

documents.title: Spreadsheets (Excel and Google Sheets)
documents.text: Spreadsheets (Excel and Google Sheets). Also known as: excel, google sheets, spreadsheet formulas, pivot tables, vlookup, xlsx. Building and using worksheets in Excel or Google Sheets: entering and formatting data, writing formulas and functions, sorting and filtering, charting, and summarizing with pivot tables. Lets you organize, analyze and present everyday data.

documents.title: Leadership
documents.text: Leadership. Also known as: leading teams, team leadership, leadership skills, leading others, leadership development, vision and influence. Covers how to set direction, motivate and influence people, and build trust and accountability in a team or organisation. Once learned, you can choose a leadership approach for a situation and guide a group toward shared goals.

documents.title: People management
documents.text: People management. Also known as: managing people, team management, managing a team, line management, first-time manager, managing direct reports. Covers the day-to-day work of managing a team: setting expectations, running one-on-ones, delegating, supporting performance and development, and handling team issues. Learners can lead direct reports effectively as a first-line manager.

documents.title: Giving and receiving feedback
documents.text: Giving and receiving feedback. Also known as: feedback skills, constructive feedback, performance feedback, critique, feedback conversations, giving criticism. A part of people management focused on delivering specific, constructive feedback and responding well to feedback from others. Once learned, you can prepare and hold feedback conversations that improve performance and keep trust intact.

documents.title: Hiring and interviewing
documents.text: Hiring and interviewing. Also known as: recruiting, recruitment, job interviewing, interview skills, talent acquisition, structured interviews, candidate selection. Covers how to run a fair, effective hiring process: defining a role, sourcing and screening candidates, conducting structured interviews, and making evidence-based offer decisions. Also covers performing well as a candidate in interviews.

documents.title: Conflict resolution
documents.text: Conflict resolution. Also known as: conflict management, dispute resolution, mediation, de-escalation, resolving disagreements, workplace conflict. Covers how to understand the causes of disagreement and work through it constructively, using techniques like active listening, reframing interests, de-escalation and mediation. Learners can handle personal and workplace conflicts toward outcomes both sides accept.

documents.title: Emotional intelligence
documents.text: Emotional intelligence. Also known as: EQ, emotional quotient, emotional intelligence skills, self-awareness and empathy, emotional awareness, emotional regulation. Covers recognising and managing your own emotions, reading other people's emotions, and using empathy and self-regulation in relationships and work. Once learned, you can respond calmly under pressure and handle interpersonal situations more skillfully.

documents.title: Time management
documents.text: Time management. Also known as: personal productivity, prioritization, task prioritization, scheduling, getting things done, productivity systems, time blocking. Planning and controlling how you spend your hours: setting priorities, scheduling, handling interruptions and avoiding procrastination. Once learned, you can build a workable planning system and reliably meet your commitments.

documents.title: Critical thinking
documents.text: Critical thinking. Also known as: logical reasoning, argument analysis, informal logic, reasoning skills, analytical thinking, logical fallacies. Covers how to evaluate claims and arguments: spotting assumptions, weighing evidence, recognizing logical fallacies, and reasoning to well-supported conclusions. Once learned, you can critique an argument and build a sound one of your own.

documents.title: Decision making
documents.text: Decision making. Also known as: decision analysis, decision science, making better decisions, choice making, decision frameworks, judgment and decision making. How to frame choices, weigh options and uncertainty, and use structured methods such as decision matrices, expected value and pre-mortems. Once you know it, you can make and justify sound decisions in work and personal situations.

documents.title: Introductory psychology
documents.text: Introductory psychology. Also known as: intro to psychology, psych 101, general psychology, psychology basics, psychology 101, intro psych. A broad introduction to how people think, feel, behave and develop, covering major areas such as learning, memory, motivation, personality, social behavior and mental health. Once learned, you can explain key theories and evaluate everyday claims about behavior.

documents.title: Cognitive biases
documents.text: Cognitive biases. Also known as: mental biases, thinking errors, heuristics and biases, confirmation bias, anchoring bias, reasoning biases. A part of introductory psychology focused on systematic errors in human judgment, such as confirmation bias, anchoring and availability. Once learned, you can spot these biases in your own and others' reasoning and use simple strategies to reduce their effect.

documents.title: Ethics
documents.text: Ethics. Also known as: moral philosophy, moral theory, applied ethics, normative ethics, metaethics, morality. Covers major ethical frameworks such as consequentialism, deontology and virtue ethics, and how to apply them to real dilemmas. Once learned, you can analyse moral problems, weigh competing arguments and justify a position clearly.

documents.title: World history
documents.text: World history. Also known as: global history, history of civilization, human history, world civilizations, history of the world. A broad survey of human history across regions and eras, from early civilizations to the modern world. Once learned, you can place major events and empires in context, trace causes and connections between societies, and interpret historical claims.

documents.title: Instructional design
documents.text: Instructional design. Also known as: instructional systems design, ISD, ADDIE, course design, learning design, curriculum design, training design. Designing effective learning experiences, from defining learning objectives and assessing learner needs to sequencing content, choosing activities, and evaluating results. Once learned, you can build a course or training program that measurably teaches what it intends to.

documents.title: Nutrition
documents.text: Nutrition. Also known as: diet science, dietetics basics, macronutrients, healthy eating, nutritional science, micronutrients. Covers how food supplies energy and nutrients, including macronutrients, vitamins, minerals, hydration and energy balance. Once learned, you can read food labels, evaluate common diet claims and plan balanced meals for your own goals.

documents.title: Strength training
documents.text: Strength training. Also known as: weight training, weightlifting, resistance training, lifting weights, barbell training, gym training, powerlifting basics. Covers the principles and practice of building muscular strength and size through resistance exercise, including core lifts, form, progressive overload, programming and recovery. A learner can design and safely follow a basic training plan.

documents.title: Mindfulness and meditation
documents.text: Mindfulness and meditation. Also known as: mindfulness, meditation, mindful meditation, breath awareness, MBSR, vipassana, zen meditation, body scan. Covers the core practices of mindfulness and meditation, including breath awareness, body scans, open monitoring and loving-kindness. Once learned, you can build a steady daily practice and use it to manage stress and attention.

documents.title: Cooking fundamentals
documents.text: Cooking fundamentals. Also known as: basic cooking, kitchen basics, culinary basics, home cooking, knife skills, how to cook. Core kitchen skills for preparing meals at home: knife work, heat control, basic cooking methods like sautéing, roasting and boiling, seasoning, and following and adapting recipes. Once learned, you can cook balanced everyday meals safely and confidently.
